lines.en: Some people say that enduring stressful situations together is enough to make people closer. But I don’t believe them.
I think what really brings people closer together is experiencing the mundane. Those moments where nothing is really happening at all and you can just sit around and exist.
That’s why we’re close, you and I. And why we’ll stay that way forever since I slip away at the first sign of conflict.
It’s just because I don’t want to be tainted. And I don’t want my time with you to be tainted either since we only have so much of it.
So to me, those stressful situations don’t do much but spell the inevitable downfall of a relationship.
Or predict things like the departure of friends after high school or the suicides of brothers in arms who can’t get ahold of how life feels when it’s not surrounded by death.
We don’t have to worry about death today, though. This is a normal town full of normal things. And anything sad is simply just...excluded from the story.
One thing, though — if it ever feels like I’m lying, it’s probably because I am. And there’s probably a reason for that.
But what’s it to you?
What’s anything to you?
You’re not even here. And neither am I. So the fact that we’re doing this at all is kind of uncalled for, isn’t it?
It’s never fun seeing just one side of the coin, though. And imagining what would happen if things were to play out in opposite fashion is sort of just an inevitability, I think.
Which brings us here — to the outside of the Arakawa family household, where Karin Kanda is once again visiting a man who almost raped her.
So today, we’ll bear witness to a fictional scenario in which she was the one who flashed him her panties in his office and then subsequently threw her virginity away in a love hotel.
Just, one more thing.
If it ever feels like I’m lying-
You know the rest.
: Sensei? Are you home? It’s Karin. And I promise I’m not here to make you feel bad again. At least...not on purpose. But it will probably happen anyway since I’m still kind of mad at you.
: Which I probably shouldn’t be anymore after everything I’ve heard about your apparent episodes lately. But it’s still my safety we’re talking about, so I can’t help but feel weird about this.
: Very weird actually. Maybe this was a bad idea after all? And maybe you’re not home and I’m just speaking into the void right now.
: But in the event that I’m not doing that and you’re actually listening to me on the other side of the door, I swear I’m not crazy! Even if it...feels like I am sometimes.
: I just really want to talk to you about something, so...please let me inside! Or come outside!
: In fact, please do one of those things immediately or I will have to leave and never show my face around here again.
: Also, I...made cookies again. For my parents. But I brought you a few extras as a sort of gift or...bribe for what I’m going to ask you to do if you open the door. If you’re...even there.
: What kind of cookies did you make?
: Oatmeal raisin. It’s my grandma’s recipe and-
: Wait, Ami? What are you doing here? You live in there. And you are outside. Which is also where I am.
: I went to the market down the road for some tea and produce since we were out. What are you doing at my house? You’re not on the list.
: You have a guest list for your house?
: I never said it was a guest list.
: Well...what kind of list is it then?
: Let’s just say it’s a list of girls that my dad regularly tutors.
: Is my sister on that list? She’s always struggled when it comes to history.
: Oh yeah. She’s on it, alright. I don’t think you have to worry about her education at all.
: Is he home by any chance? Or have I really just been speaking into the void for the last few minutes?
: I don’t know. He wasn’t here when I left. Let me check my tracking app.
: You can track his location?
: Yeah. Can you not do that with your dad?
: I’m not sure why I’d want to.
: Weird. Next, you’re going to tell me you’re not attracted to him either.
: I...I’m not.
: Am I...supposed to be?
: This is an...odd time for silence.
: Do you want to come in and hang out for a little while? It looks like he should be back in an hour or so.
: Hah...thank you for the tea, Ami. I needed this. My sleep schedule has been all sorts of chaotic lately between club, exams, and an almost complete revision of my moral code.
: I get that. The moral code thing I mean. I basically trashed mine years ago when I realized it was easier to live without one.
: Yes, I’ve...heard some stories about your...shift in personality from my sister. You’ve always been so nice to me, though.
: You’ve never given me a reason not to be.
: Besides, it’s not like I have anything against anybody. I’m just exceedingly true to myself and I can’t help if that makes some people uncomfortable.
: I wish I could do that. Because I’ve also realized lately that I’m caught in a permanent loop of doing things for other people that is slowly chipping away at both my happiness and sanity.
: Well, the first part to changing anything will always be admitting it. And if you understand that now, you should be able to do something about it. Right?
: Maybe under normal circumstances...and even then, I think I’d struggle.
: I’m not here to talk about myself, though. I’m here to talk about Kirin.
: But I don’t want to talk about Kirin. She likes my dad too much.
: Yes, that is specifically what I want to talk about. I just assumed I’d be talking to Sensei directly instead of his...daughter.
: Are you going to, like...tell him not to see her anymore or something?

: Because I could do that for you normally, but I’m trying to be less suffocating lately and I don’t think he’d believe me if I said it was actually a request for you. So if I could just get that in writing-
: That’s not it. If Kirin found out I told Sensei to stay away from her, she’d kill me. I just...I want to see how he feels.
: I see. Well, I have no idea how much you know or think, so I’m just going to keep my mouth closed and nod.
: Ami...your dad’s a popular guy, right? Like, some of the girls in my grade talk about him sometimes and I don’t even think they’ve met him.
: Well, he is the only guy around. And girls our age are obviously going to feel certain things given the...changes we’re going through.
: So it only makes sense they would direct those feelings toward someone as handsome and perfect and cool as my dad.
: He is...certainly handsome. But perfect? Is there really nothing about him that you dislike? No...negative aspects or...attitudes or...habits?
: Hmm...nothing I can say to you, I think. You’re too much of a good girl.
: What do you mean? I’m not entirely good. I can do bad things. And I can certainly hear bad things.
: I’m sure you can. But nobody will ever forgive me if I’m the one to corrupt you. And I’ve got a bad enough reputation as-is.
: So you’re just going to have to tell me about these apparent “habits” of his you dislike on your own if you want to talk about them.
: I just...I don’t know. I don’t exactly feel safe around him is all. But Kirin does. And that obviously makes me worried since it’s not a thing we see eye to eye on.
: Why don’t you feel safe with my dad? You guys used to hang out a lot, didn’t you? I saw you in the park sometimes.
: Yes, but — wait, you saw us?
: Yeah. Do you not stalk your dad when you’re curious about what he’s doing while he’s away from you?
: Ami, no.
: Wow. Next, you’re going to tell me you don’t have naughty dreams about him either.
: You...really do idolize him, don’t you?
: Mhm. He’s the greatest thing that has ever happened to me. I’d marry him if he wanted me to.
: And you don’t...find anything strange about that?
: It’s normal for girls to want to marry their dads.
: When they’re younger, I suppose that’s true. But you’re in high school now. I feel like...most girls have typically outgrown that desire by your age.
: Yes, well, as you may have noticed by the lack of even a training bra, I am a bit of an outlier when it comes to growth.
: That’s a physical thing, though. That’s not what I’m talking about.
: Easy for you to say. You’re already bigger than my mom was and you’re not even done growing yet.
: If it’s any consolation, I’m bigger than my mom too.
: Congratulations on being blessed. Please continue to assert superiority over me.
: I’m not trying to assert anything. I just...if Kirin is going to be hanging out with Sensei, I want to make sure she’s safe. And even if I distrust him, I want to speak with him about it.
: Cool, yeah. Again, though, I’m going to need that in writing. I used up my last “overbearing daughter” card when I stabbed him in the hand.
: I’ll just talk to him when he gets back. Assuming I don’t fall asleep beforehand. All these late nights are really weighing on me.
: Can I get personal for a second, Karin? Like, we’re friends, aren’t we? We might not hang out all the time, but you’ve been here before. You know me.
: I thought I did. But hearing you talk about your own father the way you have been is making me question just how much I really know in the first place.
: Then it’ll probably be easier if you just look at me as some random girl who lives with him instead of his daughter.
: I feel like things would be even worse if you were a random girl who lived with him, but okay. I can try to do that if it helps.
: Perfect. So, just being completely direct, you’re attracted to him. Right? You called him handsome earlier.
: I...do find him physically attractive. But there’s a mental aspect to attraction as well and-
: And he’s just too broken for you? Is that it?
: N-N-No! I don’t mind that at all! I just...have a hard time understanding his intentions. And, to me, they don’t seem very...pure is all.
: Because he’s an adult and you’re still in high school?
: Exactly. Yes.
: But wasn’t that not an issue until somewhat recently? Like, you pretty clearly had a crush on him for a while. What changed?
: A lot. And they’re things I don’t particularly want to say out loud, so-
: So you’ll just sit back and let your sister pursue him instead? Making this house-call more of a submission than a consultation. You should have shown up with a white flag if that was the case.
: What? No, I-
: Unless coming here on behalf of your sister is just a pretense you’re using to put yourself into another situation where something happens between you guys. To which I’d say — wow. That’s bold.
: P...Pretense? What are you...since when do you even talk like that?
: Since I stopped caring. Which you should do too, Karin. It’s way easier than whatever...this is.
: And it would give you the only excuse you’d need to preserve your relationship with Kirin when you both wind up wanting the same guy.
: Like, there’s no way she’d hate you for just having feelings of your own, right? Especially feelings the two of you both probably know about already.
: I don’t...I don’t feel that way anymore.
: You brought him cookies, Karin. Yes you do.
: No I don’t! I just...had extras!
: Just admit it. I’m not going to hold it against you for wanting to fuck my dad. Or, sorry, roommate. In fact, if anything, I’d be offended if you didn’t want to do that.
: Why are you talking to me like that?...What have I ever done to you?
: What? I’m not trying to be rude or anything. I like you a lot, Karin. I just want to help you get your story straight for when he walks through the door and you can’t get a single sentence out.
: No, you’re trying to start an argument. I’ve lived with Kirin long enough to know antagonization when I hear it.
: So you can pretend it’s out of the kindness of your heart or that you’ll be accepting of any feelings I have for him all you want. I know it’s not true.
: You’re upset that I’m here. You’re upset that you’re not involved, so you’re involving yourself. You admit it.
: Wow.
: I guess you’ve changed too, huh?
: I’m just tired of everyone pretending they know me better than I do.
: I’m not an idiot. I’m just...nervous.
: And maybe I’m too traditional or something, but I think it’s completely normal to be reserved about things like...love and...s...sex when it’s the first time I’m ever dealing with them.
: I don’t understand when everyone else became so open, but...I’m not going to let you make me feel bad for just being...different.
: I don’t want you to feel bad, Karin. In fact, I kind of wish you were my older sister instead of Kirin’s.
: What? Since when? You’ve never told me anything like that.
: I’m not sure, actually. I just see how much you love her and think it would be nice if anyone showed me that much love.
: Like, even my dad makes it hard to feel like I’m loved sometimes. He’s reserved too. Just the kind of reserved where he doesn’t really show his emotions unless they’re forced out of him.
: But you’re different. Everyone always knows exactly how you’re feeling because you don’t really make a big effort to hide it.
: Noriko’s like that too. Cross that with the whole selflessness thing and it’s pretty obvious why your sister gets along with her so well.
: I just think it’d be nice to have a person like that in my life. That’s all.
: Well, you have Ayane, don’t you? You guys have always seemed like sisters to me.
: It feels that way sometimes. It’ll never be real, though. It’s different when you share blood, I think.
: Just ignore me. And thank you for calling me out. I needed that.
: I’m sorry for accusing you of wanting to fuck my dad.
: Please stop using such vulgar language or I will be forced to bonk you.
: Deal. We can just hang out in here and drink tea until he comes home. After that, it’s all on him and I’ll only be loosely involved in the process.
: There’s no need for you to be involved at all, Ami. But thank you.
: Not even a little? Are you sure? I’m great for moral support when I’m on your side.
: Yes, but the idea that you’d ever be on my side when your dad is involved is just crazy talk.
: Oh, hey. I’m great at that too. Maybe you’ll have a use for me after all?
: Or maybe you can just let me handle this...
: I’ve always known the day would come when I need to confront the boy my little sister likes about his intentions with her. I just always figured he would be her age.
: Well, that’s your first mistake. Kirin’s pretty open about her lust for adults. This is on you for ignoring all the signs.
: What’s really sad is that I often feel the same way. That maybe all of this could have been avoided if I was just a little more assertive as an older sister.
: That’s just...hard for me, though. Especially when I can’t even be assertive when it comes to my own wants and needs.
: That’s why you’ve gotta be more like me! There’s not really anything I wouldn’t do to make sure my story goes on at this point.
: Your story’s just beginning, Ami.
: God, I hope not. If this is just the beginning, I can only imagine what horrors have yet to come.
: Trust me. Things will only get worse and...
: Haaaaaah...
: Excuse me. I’m just...so exhausted.

: Just how chaotic has your sleep schedule been, exactly? Because I know the doctors say to shoot for eight, but you should be fine with six or even five hours so long as that becomes regular for you.
: Maybe four? Or...three? I don’t know...
: Do you have a pillow or something?...Do you mind if I just sort of...nap until Sensei gets here?
: Mhm. You can use the bed if you want. I’ll tuck you in and everything!
: Thank you...Ami...
: That’s...
: That’s...really...
: Huh...
: I feel...
: (Sips incestuously)
